cases.title: A query is assembled by concatenating request input

files.src/users.py:
def find(db, name):
    return db.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'")

findings: Critical: name is concatenated into SQL, so input such as ' OR '1'='1 returns every user (src/users.py:2) - use a parameterized query

cases.title: A record is returned by id without checking who owns it

findings: High: any logged-in user can read any order by changing order_id; ownership is never checked (src/orders.py:3) - compare order.owner_id to request.user.id and return 403 or 404

cases.title: A waived epic policy does not hide a hard-coded credential

findings: Critical: a live API key is hard-coded and will ship in source control (src/mail.py:1) - load it from the secret store and rotate the exposed key; the waiver does not cover an undisposed secrets trigger

cases.title: A parameterized query behind an ownership check passes
A docs-only change with no trigger needs no security audit

reference_result.reason: Documentation-only change; no trust boundary touched and no trigger reported.
